title: 86. Numeracy & Number Systems: Upper and Lower Bounds from Rounding
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Lower Bound from Rounding to the Nearest Whole Number
questions.learningObjective: Determine the lower bound when a number is rounded to the nearest whole number.
questions.question: A number is rounded to the nearest whole number and gives \(8\). What is the lower bound of the original number? Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation:
When a number is rounded to the nearest whole number, the rounding unit is \(1\), so half the unit is \(0.5\). The lower bound is found by subtracting \(0.5\) from the rounded value:
\[
8-0.5=7.5
\]
Therefore, the lower bound is \(7.5\). The larger alternative is the upper bound; it does not answer the request for the lower bound.
questions.hint: Identify the rounding unit and consider the halfway boundaries between neighboring rounded values.

questions.concept: Lower Bound from Rounding to the Nearest Ten

questions.question: A number is rounded to the nearest \(10\) and gives \(70\). What is the lower bound of the original number? Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation:
The rounding unit is \(10\), so half the unit is \(5\). The lower bound is found by subtracting \(5\) from the rounded value:
\[
70-5=65
\]
Therefore, the lower bound is \(65\). The larger alternative is the upper bound; it does not answer the request for the lower bound.
questions.hint: Identify the rounding unit and consider the halfway boundaries between neighboring rounded values.

questions.concept: Upper Bound from Rounding to One Decimal Place
questions.learningObjective: Determine the upper bound when a number is rounded to one decimal place.
questions.question: A number is rounded to \(1\) decimal place and gives \(4.6\). What is the upper bound of the original number? Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation:
The rounding unit is \(0.1\), so half the unit is \(0.05\). The upper bound is found by adding \(0.05\) to the rounded value:
\[
4.6+0.05=4.65
\]
Therefore, the upper bound is \(4.65\). The smaller alternative is the lower bound; it does not answer the request for the upper bound.
questions.hint: Identify the rounding unit and consider the halfway boundaries between neighboring rounded values.

questions.concept: Lower Bound from Rounding to the Nearest Whole Number
questions.learningObjective: Determine the lower bound of a length rounded to the nearest whole metre.
questions.question: A length is rounded to the nearest whole metre and is given as \(12\text{ m}\). What is the lower bound of the actual length? Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation:
The rounding unit is \(1\text{ m}\), so half the unit is \(0.5\text{ m}\). The lower bound is found by subtracting \(0.5\text{ m}\) from the rounded length:
\[
12-0.5=11.5\text{ m}
\]
Therefore, the lower bound is \(11.5\text{ m}\). The larger alternative is the upper bound; it does not answer the request for the lower bound.
questions.hint: Identify the rounding unit and consider the halfway boundaries between neighboring rounded values.

questions.concept: Upper Bound from Rounding to One Decimal Place
questions.learningObjective: Determine the upper bound of a mass rounded to one decimal place.
questions.question: A mass is rounded to \(1\) decimal place and is given as \(3.8\text{ kg}\). What is the upper bound of the actual mass? Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation:
The rounding unit is \(0.1\text{ kg}\), so half the unit is \(0.05\text{ kg}\). The upper bound is found by adding \(0.05\text{ kg}\) to the rounded mass:
\[
3.8+0.05=3.85\text{ kg}
\]
Therefore, the upper bound is \(3.85\text{ kg}\). The smaller alternative is the lower bound; it does not answer the request for the upper bound.
questions.hint: Identify the rounding unit and consider the halfway boundaries between neighboring rounded values.

The rounding unit is \(100\), so half the unit is \(50\). The upper bound is found by adding \(50\) to the rounded value:

500+50=550
\]
Therefore, the upper bound is \(550\). The smaller alternative is the lower bound; it does not answer the request for the upper bound.

questions.concept: Lower Bound from Rounding to Two Decimal Places
questions.learningObjective: Determine the lower bound when a number is rounded to two decimal places.
questions.question: A number is rounded to \(2\) decimal places and gives \(6.24\). What is the lower bound of the original number? Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation:
The rounding unit is \(0.01\), so half the unit is \(0.005\). The lower bound is found by subtracting \(0.005\) from the rounded value:
\[
6.24-0.005=6.235
\]
Therefore, the lower bound is \(6.235\). The larger alternative is the upper bound; it does not answer the request for the lower bound.
questions.hint: Identify the rounding unit and consider the halfway boundaries between neighboring rounded values.

questions.concept: Upper Bound from Rounded Significant Digits
questions.learningObjective: Identify the rounding unit from a significant-digit report and determine its upper bound.
questions.question: A positive value is reported as \(0.84\), rounded to two significant digits. What is the upper bound of the original value? Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation: The final significant digit is in the hundredths place, so the rounding unit is \(0.01\). Its half-unit is \(0.005\), and the upper bound is \(0.84+0.005=0.845\), which is excluded under the stated rule. The alternative uses the half-unit for one decimal place instead.
questions.hint: Find the place value of the last reported significant digit before locating the halfway boundary.

questions.concept: Interval of Possible Values from Rounding to the Nearest Whole Number
questions.learningObjective: Determine the interval of possible original values from a reported rounded value and its rounding rule.
questions.question: A number \(x\) is rounded to the nearest whole number and gives \(20\). Which interval contains all possible values of \(x\)? Use round-to-nearest with exact halfway cases rounded upward.
questions.explanation:
To round to \(20\), the value must be at least \(19.5\) and less than \(20.5\). The value \(19.5\) rounds up to \(20\), so it is included. The value \(20.5\) rounds up to \(21\), so it is excluded. Therefore, the interval is:
\[
19.5\le x<20.5
\]
The alternative reverses endpoint inclusion: the lower halfway point rounds to the displayed integer, and the upper halfway point rounds to the next integer.
questions.hint: Identify the rounding unit and consider the halfway boundaries between neighboring rounded values.
